title: Leaving for the Army; Shadow Wilson subs; Walter Page sent home
summary: He left the Lincoln Hotel for the Army, with Shadow Wilson playing for a week, while Walter Page was sent home to settle family troubles.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: That was when you went in the Army?
I left from there to go in the Army, because I left and I had Shadow to play in my place for -

Shadow Wilson. I had him to play in my place for one week because I went down to Washington. They wanted me to go into the Navy Band but Mr. Glenn Miller had sent a brown envelope- you know, Glenn had the overlay for the musicians going into the Army and he was placing various peoples. Shadow was there, Rodney Richardson was on bass,
you see, because we had sent Big'Un home.
Well, we sent Big'Un home for a rest, you know, he went home to take care of his family.
Having family problems huh. This was about 1943 or 1944?

This was in '44. Course he was on salary. He could just go home, do what he wanted to do. He didn't have to worry about nothing; his salary went on anyway, you know. So he was trying to get his family life straightened.
